findings.reason: a node implementing §16's three named call sites leaves this fourth resolver unconsolidated, so the section's stated outcome ("One owner resolves a repository to its projects") is not achieved and the worktree defect persists on the run-rebuild path.
findings.text: §16 enumerates the resolver population as three (`_repository_owning_projects` in `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py`, the inline lookup in `shadow_source`, and `_resolved_node_scope_entries`), excluding `project_mount_repository` because it resolves the other way; but `_project_for_repository` in `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:60` is a fourth site resolving a repository path to its owning project in the same direction, called from the run-rebuild path at promotion_records.py:107, and its docstring claims identity semantics ("by repository identity so a linked worktree resolves to the same project as its main checkout") while its body compares plain resolved paths (`repository_root.resolve() == target`, lines 68-75) — so it fails on a linked worktree exactly as §16 says `shadow_source` does

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol and file `§16` cites resolves: `_repository_owning_projects`/`_refuse_a_foreign_repository` (reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:518,540), `shadow_source`/`mounted_repository_projects` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:198,205), `_resolved_node_scope_entries` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:896), `project_mount_repository` (reckon/crew/dispatch_sections.py:42), and the resolver's home `routing.py` beside `mounted_repository_projects` (reckon/crew/routing.py:3241), whose `from reckon.crew.node import …` at line 38 is why the resolver cannot live in `node.py`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — `§16` names a measurable check and a declared negative control: a temporary mounted repository plus a linked worktree with no `crew.json`, asserting the resolver names the mounted project and that `shadow_source` searches it, and that this fails on main where `shadow_source` keys the mount map by plain `resolve()` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:204-205).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the section writes no evidence into a scratch path; the plan's landing records stay on the durable `/reckon/evidence/archive/lane-and-model-routing-landed.html` record.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol; the cited names are existing code identifiers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — `§16` states the repository-path→projects resolution has three spellings, but a fourth live spelling exists that it does not name.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — `§16` carries one deliverable, one owner for the repository-path→projects resolution.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `s16` is a follow-on of `§10`'s review and the open followup `f-lmr-009` (plan line 209) correctly orders `§14` before `§16` on their shared write path `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py`; no `depends-on` entry is required because their only coupling is file contention.
